MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
February 4, 2013

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m. on Monday,
February 4, 2013, in the Council Chambers, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Councilmember Savidan led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to the roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Community Services Director McPherron,
Public Works Director Damasse, Administrative Services Director Chavez, and Assistant City
Clerk Shumway.

2. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Gazeley seconded
the motion, which carried unanimously.

3. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that the Los Angeles County Sheriff's
Department had purchased a Mobile Command Center for the Lomita Sheriff's Station, which
will be delivered in May 2013. City Manager Rock added that Captain Bolin requested Los
Angeles County cover the additional expenses for equipment for the Mobile Command Center,
which are estimated at around $20,000.

City Manager Rock also informed City Council that he discussed the helicopter noise issue with
Captain Bolin, and that both he and Captain Bolin will be meeting soon with the Coast Guard
Commander regarding the issue.

City Manager Rock announced that the Special City Council Meeting / Strategic Planning
Workshop has been scheduled for February 13, 2013, and will start at 4 p.m., in order to discuss
the City's mission, vision, and core values, as well as review the mid-year budget and discuss
issue papers. City Manager Rock added that the meeting is open to the public.

City Attorney Hogin stated for the record that the City Council had Special City Council Meeting
  Page 1 of 1
 at 6 p.m., and convened to closed session at 6:01 p.m. City Attorney Hogin announced that
there were two potential litigation items on the agenda, as well as the overcharge of property tax
that the City is pursuing reimbursement on, but no reportable action was taken on these items.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina stated that he received some phone calls from residents that play Bingo
at the Recreation Center on Thursdays complaining that the room was cold; Councilmember
Traina asked staff to accommodate their request for a suitable temperature. Councilmember
Traina also stated that he received a complaint from a resident regarding the taste of the water,
and since the water blending process has not started yet, he asked if staff had received similar
complaints from others. Public Works Director Damasse responded that only one complaint had
been received, and that the reason for the poor taste was that the property owner’s own water
heater had not been flushed for over seven years.

Councilmember Savidan thanked City Manager Rock for looking into the helicopter noise issue
and asked that a meeting be scheduled with the subcommittee members, with a possible
invitation to the Coast Guard Commander.

Councilmember Sanchez announced that the Community Emergency Response Training
(CERT) dates had been finalized, with the first training class scheduled for Saturday, April 13,
2013. Councilmember Sanchez added that the training dates will be held on three consecutive
Saturdays, and will be for seven hours each.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Cindy Segawa, Lomita resident, stated that she had not yet received a credit on her water bill,
as was stated during previous City Council meetings, but did receive a flyer with her new bill
indicating that she would only be charged at the Tier 1 rate. Ms. Segawa asked if she would be
receiving a credit on her account. City Manager Rock asked Ms. Segawa to meet with
Administrative Services Director Chavez regarding her issue.

Scott Gobble, Representative of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, thanked Mayor Estrada
and, Councilmembers Savidan and Sanchez, for attending the Annual Lomita Chamber of
Commerce Installation Dinner. Mr. Gobble also informed those in attendance that the
Chamber's next Business Mixer will take place on Thursday, February 28, 2013, at the Lomita
Magnet School, from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. Mr. Gobble added that the March Business Mixer had
been scheduled to take place at the Lomita Library, with proceeds from the mixer to be donated
to the Library.

In response to Councilmember Gazeley's question about whether power outages were possible
this year due to the closure of the Newport Beach power plant and continuing issues at the San
Onofre nuclear power plant, Mr. Gobble explained that the San Onofre Nuclear Generation
Station will be reopened, and will operate at 70% capacity for five months to see if there are any
degradation issues concerning the tubes and cooling system. Mr. Gobble added that power
outages were not anticipated for this year given conservation efforts, new renewable energy,
and an operational San Onofre Nuclear Generation Station.

  Page 2 of 2
 6. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Savidan
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously, except that Councilmember Sanchez's vote
was not counted on item #6.J, as he had previously recused himself due to the fact that he lives
within 500 feet of the subject property.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Regular City Council meeting held on
  January 22, 2013, the Special City Council meeting held on January 22, 2013, and the
  Regular meeting of the Lomita Community Development Advisory Board held on January
  22, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  d. Monthly Report for Economic Development and Information Technology activities.
  RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  f. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Monthly Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  h. Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  i. Report submitting a professional services agreement with Veronica Tam and Associates to
  prepare the fifth revision to the Housing Element in an amount not to exceed $21,550.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  j. Settlement Agreement with the Islamic Center of the South Bay (ICSB) and Agreed Order
  with the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ). RECEIVE AND FILE.

  k. Establishment of a Nuisance Abatement Street Tree List. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

7.  COMMISSION APPOINTMENTS

Councilmembers Traina, Sanchez, and Gazeley nominated Gia Stokes to fill the vacancy on the
Public Safety and Traffic Commission.

Gia Stokes was appointed to the Public Safety and Traffic Commission.

8.  RECORDS MANAGEMENT POLICY AND RECORDS RETENTION

Assistant City Clerk Shumway stated that the creation of the records retention policy and
records retention schedules was a six to seven month process that involved a collaborative
effort between all department directors, staff, and the City Attorney. According to Assistant City
  Page 3 of 3
 Clerk Shumway, the City does not currently have an established records retention policy or
retention schedules, but the adoption of the prepared records retention policy and records
retention schedules would provide staff with the proper tools for the efficient management of City
records. Assistant City Clerk Shumway stated that having a records retention policy and
retention schedules would benefit the City by allowing for better control over the creation and
growth of records, improving productivity, preserving the “historic memory” of the organization
through the archival of records, and by allowing for the disposition of records that are no longer
needed. Furthermore, Assistant City Clerk Shumway stated that the City would also benefit
through the more efficient utilization of space within the City, and through the elimination of
outside storage costs by bringing all City records in-house.

Assistant City Clerk Shumway stated that City Council would make the final decision regarding
the destruction of records, after records destruction requests have been reviewed by the City
Clerk and City Attorney. According to Assistant City Clerk Shumway, if Council approves the
proposed records retention policy and records retention schedules, then a resolution for the
destruction of certain City records would be presented to City Council in March 2013.

In response to Councilmember Traina’s question on whether any City records were had been
previously destroyed, Assistant City Clerk Shumway responded that in the past several
resolutions were approved by City Council for the destruction of records, however, the City
Attorney reviewed each of those requests in accordance with code requirements and other
regulations. Assistant City Clerk Shumway added that records retention schedules provide clear
direction to City staff, and establishes necessary retention requirements in one document.

Councilmember Traina asked whether the City currently pays for the off-site storage of records,
and if so, what was the associated cost. Assistant City Clerk Shumway responded that the City
pays roughly $2,500 a year. Furthermore, Assistant City Clerk Shumway added that the quote
received for records destruction was $200, for up to 400 boxes.

Councilmember Savidan complimented staff on the creation of such an extensive policy, and
noted that the City has needed this for a long time.

Councilmember Traina moved to accept staff's recommendation.  Councilmember Savidan
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

9.  CYPRESS WATER PRODUCTION FACILITY OFFLINE TESTING

Lynn Grijalva, Consultant from Hazen and Sawyer, reported to City Council that 139 people had
participated in the water tasting survey. Ms. Grijalva stated the staff utilized a variety of different
community and City-related meetings and events to conduct water tastings, in which residents
were offered to taste three water samples, and rate those samples over several categories.
According to Ms. Grijalva, the results of the survey were as follows: 88% stated that the 50/50%
blend was acceptable; 80% thought that the Metropolitan water was acceptable; and 64% of
those surveyed found that the 60/40% blend was acceptable. Ms. Grijlva concluded that based
on the water tasting survey results, most of those responding found that the blended water
tasted good, and were not able to distinguish between blended water and the water they were
currently receiving through the Metropolitan Water District (MWD).

In response to Councilmember Sanchez’s question on whether improvements have been made,
or need to be made, to the Cypress Water Production Facility, Public Works Director Damasse
  Page 4 of 4
 responded that the work is still on-going, and that they are currently waiting for some supplies
and some piping to be completed.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the report, and to move forward with the water
blending. Councilmember Savidan seconded the motion. Councilmember Traina asked to
include in the motion that City Council be notified if any complaints are received.
Councilmember Sanchez seconded Councilmember Traina’s request, and suggested that staff
provide a bi-monthly report regarding any complaints received, the location of those complaints,
and how City staff resolved the complaint. The motion carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 7:40 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
